cases.name: Luz Hernández
cases.about: She was a native of the Dominican Republic and a kindergarten teacher at the BelovED Charter School in Jersey City, NJ. Hernandez's cousin, Yajaira Germosen, said in a tearful interview that, 'She was kind. She was a beautiful person." Another unnamed cousin told NBC New York, 'We love her, her family, the friends. She was an amazing girl and it’s so unfair somebody takes away the life from her. Why? 'She was one of the best teachers, everybody loves her, all the kids. It’s just like, so complicated to think about this. We just want justice,' they continued. Her brother Christiano Hernandez told CBS New York, 'She loved kids. She became a teacher because she loved being around kids.' BeloveED founder Bret Schundler told NJ.com, 'People loved her. She was a wonderful coworker. She was a beloved member of the BelovED family. People are feeling devastated by this.' Hernandez had been teaching at the school since graduating from Saint Peter's University in New Brunswick, New Jersey, in 2017. Two of her children are students at the school.
cases.narrative: On 2/11/2023, her body was found buried in a shallow grave in an industrial section of Kearny, NJ. She died of blunt force trauma to the head and compressions to the neck.

cases.name: Norelis "Nora" Mendoza
cases.about:
She grew up in Jersey City and lived in Lindenwold at the time of her death. Her Go Fund Me said, "Our beloved Norelis found passion in helping others and dedicated her career to the medical field. Her smile was infectious, She was a beacon of light and would help anyone she could. "

Her obituary said, "On Saturday May 13, 2023, at approximately 10:22 PM Norelis left her mother's home In Jersey City, expressing her love and that she would see her soon. That was the last time that she was seen by a loved one.

Norelis never returned home and was reported missing the very next day on Sunday, May 14th which was Mother’s Day. The authorities got involved but more importantly it was the help from social media to make our political leaders aware that she was not just a picture of a missing person but she was a real person. A mother, daughter, sister, aunt, niece, cousin, and friend. On Tuesday, May 16th they were able to get a break in her case to find camera footage of where she was during the time of telling her mother bye for the last time and also the person she was with during her last hours and minutes. On Wednesday, May 17th our prayers of bringing Norelis (Nora) home safely ended in tragedy for all. Norelis was found around 11:30am in between the city limits of Jersey City and Bayonne. The family is finding solace that she is now with God. Our beloved Norelis found passion in helping others and dedicated her career to the medical field. Her smile was infectious, She was a beacon of light and would help anyone she could. We are left with her beautiful daughters and will raise them with her legacy of love and kindness. They are one and three years old and need all the love and support they can get. She enjoyed being a mom and did everything for her daughters. During this whole ordeal her daughters have cried for her everyday. This has been a senseless act of violence and her girls have been ripped from having their mom on this earth with them. We are all beyond devastated and suffering. Mother’s Day is a joyous time to celebrate and her girls and family will forever live through the pain of what happened on this day. We are now asking for anyone to help in anyway possible so that the family can take care of her daughters as she would have loved to do herself. We all want to honor her as a mother and carry out the plan she had for her girls.

Norelis is deeply loved , We will not stop protecting, supporting and loving your girls. We won’t stop until we get justice for you. Rest in paradise Beautiful Angel we will take it from here with everyone’s help.

Watch over us."
cases.narrative:
On 5/17/2023, her body was found in a wooded area of Route 440, near Kennedy Boulevard. Her autopsy noted injuries consistent with a pedestrian struck by a vehicle: fractured scapulas and pelvis, and injuries to lung and avulsion injuries.

He allegedly ran her over with a pickup truck that she had purchased for him, killing her. After a night that started with a trip to the American Dream mall, followed by drinks at a Jersey City bar, and then an early morning meal at McDonald’s on Communipaw Avenue, Mallard drove Mendoza to the area of Burma Road and Thomas McGovern Avenue, near Liberty State Park, at 4:20 a.m. on May 14 and struck her twice with her Dodge Ram pickup truck. After the first strike Mendoza jumped up and tried to run, authorities said in the criminal complaint. That’s when Mallard made a U-turn and ran over her again, leaving Mendoza unresponsive.

cases.name: Temara Sarafina King
cases.about:
She was a public school teacher. King was an "outstanding educator and dedicated faculty member," at Public School Number 5, Jersey City Public Schools Superintendent Dr. Norma Fernandez said in a statement.

Her obituary said, "Temara, who was affectionately known as Sara to her close family and friends, was educated in the Jersey City Public School system. She attended Dr. Ercel F. Webb Elementary School, Public School No. 22. She then attended James J. Ferris High School, where she served as a member of the student council and played on the basketball team. Temara pursued higher education at New Jersey City University (NJCU) where she earned a Bachelor of Arts degree in Early Childhood Education and held a Teacher Certification for Preschool to 3rd grade, Special Education and Sociology. She also attained a Master of Education degree in Special Education from Grand Canyon University. In 2022, Temara completed the Learning Disabilities Teacher Consultant certification program at NJCU.

 

Temara followed in the footsteps of her late grandmother, Marian King, who was also a Jersey City Public School Educator. She taught Special Education and worked primarily with students with Autism Spectrum Disorder. Temara spent most of her professional career at Dr. Michael Conti School, Public School No.5, where she also served as their union representative for the Jersey City Education Association. She worked with the C.A.S.P.E.R. aftercare program and even spent her summers teaching students at Regional Day School. Additionally, she provided developmental intervention services to children in the Early Intervention Program. Temara is revered by her colleagues and parents in the Public School No. 5 community as a phenomenal educator whose smile brightened every room she entered. Temara’s passion for teaching and dedication to her craft did not go unnoticed. In 2018, she was presented with the award for Inclusion Teacher of the Year, by the New Jersey Coalition for Inclusive Education. She was also honored as Exemplary Educator of the Year by the New Jersey Department of Education in 2022. Temara’s final educational pursuit secured her promotion as a Learning Disabilities Teacher Consultant at William L. Dickinson High School, which she spoke about with great joy and anticipation. Unfortunately, her prospective students and colleagues will never get the chance to experience her radiant energy and educational expertise.

 

Out of her many talents, Temara was a master of time. She was always punctual and managed to balance her work and home life with perfection. Outside of the classroom, she shared her love for fitness, which fueled her desire to pursue entrepreneurship. In 2021, Temara opened a dance/fitness studio in Jersey City. She hosted boxing, Zumba, African dance and boot camp classes. She also found ways to intertwine her love of arts & crafts, as she hosted painting events and pop-up shops. Temara collaborated with her sister, Asha, to create Fine & Fit under Susie’s Daughters, LLC, which were brands associated with health and wellness. She aspired to become a certified Zumba instructor and to reopen an even bigger and better dancefit studio. Her love for dance began at a young age with the creation of the LG steppers alongside her cousins. The group danced to all of Bad Boy’s greatest hits, and everyone who knew Temara knew she loved P. Diddy!

Temara also loved her family fiercely. You could count on her to show up for any and every occasion. She was the glue that held everyone and everything together. She professed her love for her family regularly, especially for her daughter, Alaysia King, who she lovingly referred to as her “Mooche.” Alaysia was truly the light of Temara’s life."
